rationale: The hard-indicator restriction genuinely converts the archive's incumbent into a within-stratum comparison that neutralizes the HML/CMA gradient the archive diagnosed, and the expression matches the hypothesis, though it remains the same two legs as "Self Funded Payout At Cheap Enterprise Value" with only the conditioning weight changed, and the 70% mass of exact zeros will make the middle of the sort degenerate.

The sign convention is internally consistent (long = expensive repurchasers, short = expensive issuers) and it is a defensible structural response to the wrong-signed +0.048 alpha of the archive's rich-valuation issuance signal, but the underlying content is close to the well-documented net-issuance/market-timing anomaly and the pairing with Signal 1 is more of a diagnostic split than a new mechanism.

Multiplying a nonnegative growth rank into a signed payout term makes the short leg "cheap, fast-growing net issuers," which is essentially the asset-growth/external-financing anomaly restated rather than a neutralization of CMA, and the long leg (cheap + high growth + large self-funded payout) is a rare corner likely to produce unstable portfolio composition.

The expression is internally inconsistent with its hypothesis: since IND_RANK is nonnegative and NEG(VOL) is nonpositive, the maximum values (~0) are attained by expensive firms regardless of financing volatility, so the long leg is dominated by high-multiple names rather than the intended cheap-and-stable firms, and financing volatility is also heavily confounded with size and general firm volatility.

The multiplicative structure is coherent here (firms near their highs correctly collapse to the uninformative middle) and a pure price-history conditioner is not spanned by FF5, but the annual-frequency 5-year drawdown is a coarse conditioner and the design sits very close to the archive's already-tested "Contrarian Buyback At Own Valuation Low," so the incremental content is modest.

target_name: Capital Return Per Sales Dollar At Cheap Value
rationale: This is a denominator swap on the archive's incumbent signal — a cosmetic variant in construction even though the stated motivation (removing price from both legs) is a legitimate diagnostic — and scaling by sales introduces its own distortions for low-sales, financial, and pre-revenue firms that a 1% winsor will not fully control.
